newsitem.title: UK: UK Conservatives barely exist in cities -- Redwood.
newsitem.headline: UK Conservatives barely exist in cities -- Redwood.

text.p: A candidate for the leadership of the opposition Conservatives admitted on Tuesday that the party was in a desperate plight and "almost doesn't exist in the great cities".

John Redwood told a news conference it was vitally important to start rehabilitating the party following its massive defeat at the May 1 general election when it won a bare quarter of the 659 seats in the House of Commons.
"It is desperate that we turn it round quickly, that we start to offer this party some leadership," Redwood, seen as the most right-wing Eurosceptic of the six candidates to replace John Major, said.
"We need a new popular Conservatism which relates to people's hopes and fears. They need to believe we care about them again," he added.
Redwood's comment about the party's weakness in major urban areas follows an election in which it failed to gain seats in any of Britain's main cities with the exception of London.
The party was also left without MPs in both Scotland and Wales.
Redwood said the Conservatives were "on the retreat even as we meet this morning" in many of the seats which had been lost at the election.
His recipe for party revival includes a greater willingness to listen to the ideas and dissatisfactions of ordinary people.
"We can show people we understand. We should start on the doorsteps. We should remind ourselves why we are in politics in the first place."

Redwood declined to comment on the tribulations of fellow leadership candidate Michael Howard, who was savaged in a parliamentary speech on Monday by Ann Widdecombe, who until the election was a junior minister under him at the Home Office.

He said he had deliberately stayed away from the House of Commons chamber while Widdecombe charged Howard with misleading parliament over the sacking of a prison governor and of the head of the prison service.
"I did not want my presence to be misconstrued at all," he said. -- London Newsroom +44 171 5427767
